name: Loire Valley

known.via: English Wikipedia "Loire Valley wine" (redirects to "Loire Valley (wine)")

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
keyfacts: The Upper Loire has Sauvignon Blanc in Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé, and the Lower Loire reaches the Atlantic through Muscadet, where Melon dominates.
In the Middle Loire, Vouvray is made from Chenin Blanc, Chinon and Saumur reds are based on Cabernet Franc, and Touraine whites are based on Sauvignon Blanc.
White wine is the largest share at about 36% of production, and Cabernet Franc, Chenin Blanc, Melon and Sauvignon Blanc are the most planted grapes.
The Loire is France's second largest region for AOP sparkling wine, after Champagne.

notes: Loire wines tend to be fruity, with fresh, crisp flavors from high acidity, especially when young.
Many go through a dumb phase between two and five years, and the best can then age 20 years.
Sweetness runs from bone dry (sec) to very sweet moelleux wines, often touched by noble rot.
Sauvignon Blanc tastes of gooseberry and grapefruit, and cool years give lighter, more mineral wines.
Loire Pinot Noir is very light in body and color, and ripe Cabernet Franc smells of raspberry and pencil shavings.

blurb.text: The wine regions along the Loire river, from Muscadet on the Atlantic coast to Sancerre in the east, with smaller vineyards further upstream in the Massif Central, such as Saint-Pourçain and Côte Roannaise.
